title: Teaching a summer jazz class at Pratt in the riot years
summary: A group of about ten musicians taught underprivileged children in a building donated at Pratt one summer under Mayor Lindsay's administration.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: But in '68 then I went back to play with Don Ewell at the Golden Nugget in Toronto, and then -- and then I started going to the Poconos -- and then we had a group that taught school for -- out in Pratt University for the summer, for the summer session, and I think --

Yeah, we had a summer class out there. That was during the days when they were, what was it called, keeping down the hot summer with the riots and stuff, and they -- we went out there to teach. They practically donated a building to us.
Oh, yeah, that was during Lindsay's administration.

donated a building for -- and they had about ten of us, Joe Bill Newman, Norris Turner and me and Heywood Henry and a bunch of us went out there and was teaching underprivileged children out there, but that did -- that only lasted one summer.
